title: Eyewitness Testimony Seven Years Later
subtitle_source: subs_resolved/0905.txt, subs_resolved/0906.txt (760 dialogue lines, full transcript read)
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran) and local police inspector Makoto Muramatsu (pure investigating-officer scaffolding, no clue-bearing edges) omitted by convention. case_type: murder (a present-day double murder covering up a seven-year-old robbery-murder). No `event` node type: actions are direct typed edges. Correction vs. old low-fidelity file (cases/ep905-906_eyewitness_testimony_seven_years_later.json): the old file's stated culprit (Ohara) and its two headline clues (planted hair failing as evidence because a convertible can't transport a body; the magnet+bottle-opener locked-room mechanism) all check out against the transcript -- no reversal needed there. However the old file was substantially incomplete: it treated Otaro only as a 'suspect' and omitted that he is himself a second murder victim; it omitted the witness Miona entirely (the actual throughline of the case -- a five-year-old who witnessed the original robbery-murder and, traumatized, spent the whole case unable to recall the culprits' faces until the finale); it left the motive as 'unspecified' when the transcript is explicit (Ohara killed reporter Kyujiro to silence blackmail over the old crime, then killed his former partner-in-crime Otaro because Otaro wanted to kill Miona to keep her from ever remembering); and it omitted nearly all the physical evidence chain (the bugged listening device, the Byun-card threat, the reversed dying-message signature, the bottle-count/cap-shape mismatch, Ohara's magnet-damaged watch). Ohara's own stated motive (protecting Miona) vs. Kogoro's counter-accusation that he had 'always planned' to murder and frame Otaro is left explicitly unresolved by the transcript itself -- both are captured in attrs/notes rather than picking one.

clues.desc: Bloody symbol at Otaro's death scene first read as the Masked Comet Byun mark, but the hand position is reversed -- it is actually Otaro's own overlapped katakana signature style ('oh' circle + 'ha' two strokes), spelling 'Ohara' as a dying message.

Seven empty beer bottles but only six bottle caps on the cow-magnet chain, and the caps show two differently shaped pry-marks -- proves a second, borrowed bottle opener was used and one cap was removed from the scene.
Ohara is seen wearing his watch on his wrist instead of his usual pocket, and glances at the wall clock right after checking it -- the watch is broken.
